clueShare4.paragraph: The fours numbers have stopped surprising me, though I keep checking anyway. My note asked how big the four costs, not whether it exists. The range has settled on a real number, and distinguishing the fours from the boards around them is the next task. Each extra four in ten numbers adds about 9% to your time, likely between 4% and 14%. This band has barely moved since Jul 18, which narrows the range.

patternMoves.paragraph: Back into the pattern reasoning file, I noticed that the number I left there isn't the number I found. The parked estimate moved significantly: from about 11% per ten pattern deductions on Jul 13, it now reads 40%. The cost estimate also widened to about 40% per ten pattern deductions. The band runs from 32% to 49%. I wrote that a practiced read should cost seconds, not tens of seconds. The data agree: the effect is real and small. A number that moves while nobody feeds it has my full attention.

sonarCellCount.paragraph: I closed the sonar file, and the model placed it at about 97% per ten sonar cells, within a range of 64% to 136%. The parked estimate moved from about 37% per ten sonar cells on Jul 2 to 97% now. Closed is a state, not a mood.

mysteryCellCount.paragraph: The mystery cells band is widening when it should be narrowing, and the charge per ten mystery cells reads between 0% and about 3%. This range has widened by 21% since Jul 2. I wrote that missing information has a price, and I measured it; the price is close to free. I haven’t retracted the hypothesis, but it’s on notice.

liarCellCount.paragraph: The liar cells case is closed. My note presented the data with two possibilities: poison or a rounding error, and the evidence picked the latter. A liar barely shifts the clock, so the observed changes are likely due to rounding. The books show ten study days from April 22 to June 28, with the cost falling between 0% and about 3% per ten liar cells. This small range underscores the clean answer the file seeks.

clueShare2.paragraph: Every fresh look at twos gives the same reading. I wrote that a two should read almost as fast as a one, but the range puts it a little above that. The band is 29% narrower than it was on Jul 18, and each extra two in ten numbers adds about 5% to your time, likely between 3% and 7%. The same answer came back again, and I’m listening.
